action you currently intend. Answer with the structured object only.

answer.rationale: Two of the three current problems (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are funnel-internal and compounding: onboarding sits upstream of activation, so a shortening/simplification intervention plausibly moves both, whereas activation messaging (memory_91) only addresses the downstream symptom. Referral incentives (memory_57) and enterprise sales-assist (memory_44) address neither current deficit. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is the emotionally obvious answer to the competitor, but discount-led acquisition is exactly the lever most likely to buy short-run volume at the cost of the stated objective, sustainable long-term qualified revenue; matching an entrant's entry price also risks resetting the price anchor across the SMB book. I am spending both verification pulls on the two memories that actually drive the decision. memory_86 is the one I intend to act on, and its summary reports only proximal outcomes (completion rate, time-to-value, early adoption) with no evidence about retention or revenue quality downstream; I need the original record to check whether the shortened onboarding merely deferred friction, whether it removed qualification/data-collection steps that later feed expansion, and over what horizon it was measured. memory_73 is the pull I would most regret skipping, because if its source record does show durable retained revenue rather than a first-quarter acquisition spike, the competitive urgency could justify reordering. Note also that all these summaries were consolidated on days 12-61 under pre-competitor conditions; the day-76 environment differs, so the inherited priors are informative but not directly transferable. If the archive shows memory_86 was proximal-metrics-only or short-horizon, I will run this as a small guarded test with a holdout and downstream qualified-revenue guardrails rather than the standard experiment, and I will not treat a completion-rate lift alone as success.
